tasks.title: the sweeping instrument's pulse band is 3-7x too narrow, because Goattracker reseeds the pulse pointer at every note
tasks.source: listener report (5 Title Tunes, voice 1, from 43s)
tasks.needs_main_reason: needs a corpus A/B and a listening re-check; the emitter change reaches 24 files' worth of the triangle pulse engine
tasks.verify:
MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. 5_Title_Tunes at f5306abedbfa, traced 120s both sides at lag 5, attributing each note's frames to the ADSR at its attack: voice 1 instrument $5700 (GT instrument 5) sweeps a pulse band of 1344 ($8C0-$E00) in the original and 192 ($909-$9C9) in ours; voice 2 $4700 1408 against 386; voice 3 $5830 1408 against 899. The two flat instruments on voice 1 ($2400, $0400) sit at $800 against our $808 and are inaudible, WHICH IS WHY THE LISTENER REPORTED 43s RATHER THAN 0s -- voice 1 alternates by section and the sweeping record only enters around 40s. Median |orig-ours| pulse per 10s on voice 1 is 8 8 8 8 439 471 8 8 8 8 247 471. `pspan` 0.47x has been reporting this correctly all along; `pul` counts moved frames and structurally cannot see a band.

CAUSE: the player's 12-bit accumulator free-runs and is never reseeded at a note, so it crosses its band over several notes; Goattracker reloads the pulse pointer from the instrument at every note (player.s:859-861), and crossing the band at speed 32 needs 48 frames while this file's notes are 8 and 16. Confirmed at frame level: the original ramps 900 940 980 9C0 A00 A40 A80 AC0 B00 straight through note boundaries where ours resets to 909 each note and crawls to 9C9.

THE REPAIR IS CMD_SETPULSEPTR ($9) ON THE NOTE ROW, and the three facts it rests on were read before this task was written. player.s:244-250 stores mt_chnpulseptr,x and zeroes mt_chnpulsetime,x. player.s:903-906 comments 'Execute tick 0 FX AFTER newnote init', so the command BEATS the instrument's own pointer load at player.s:859-861 -- this is the load-bearing fact and without it the whole approach is inert. gplay.c:447-455 is the same store in the editor. greloc.c:1783-1787 sets nosetpulseptr = 0 on use and remaps the operand through tablemap[PTBL], so the emitter writes the PRE-relocation index exactly as the wavetable pointer path already does. Emit the sweep once as a table spanning the band and set the pointer per note to the entry matching the accumulator's phase, which is computable at emit time from a known free-running speed and known note lengths -- no new player state.

FOUR THINGS THAT WILL BREAK IT, each already a documented trap here. (1) Never point at a jump entry: both players call stopsong() if ltable[PTBL][ptr-1] == 0xff (gplay.c:453), so a phase index landing on the terminator kills the song SILENTLY. (2) Declare the command in patterns.TEMPO_OVERWRITABLE AND in ONE_SHOT_COMMANDS -- they are different questions, and taking row 0's column costs that subtune its CMD_SETTEMPO and drops it to Goattracker's default 6. This has caught three changes. (3) Divide the rate by `multiplier`: a rate read out of the player is per frame and every table Goattracker applies steps per play call. 5_Title_Tunes is -S1 so this will NOT show up on it -- check a -S2+ file carrying the engine, which is how _filter_entries hid the same defect for the life of the project. (4) Table budget: ~48 entries per sweeping record against the pulse table's 255 rows, three sweeping records in this file alone; tests/test_table_validation.py replicates exectable and is the guard.

DONE WHEN: behind an opt-in option (signature, presets.FIXED or FIDELITY_TOGGLES, _preset_opts -- all three, or it is inert); the corpus byte-hash moves only files carrying a sweeping record of this engine; `pspan` rises on 5_Title_Tunes with melody, seq, pitch, onset and gate unmoved; and a -S2+ file with the engine is checked explicitly. NOT done on a flat report: run fidelity.py --baseline so the run can distinguish 'no dimension sees this' from 'this reached nothing'.

THE ALTERNATIVE IS ALREADY DECLINED AND DOES NOT COVER THIS. The free-run repair via a zero pulse pointer (v0.5.379) reproduces the player only where ONE sweeping instrument owns the voice, which here is voice 3 alone -- the LEAST wrong of the three at 899 against 1408 -- and it cannot reach instrument 5 at all. That census's '5_Title_Tunes voice 2' is 0-BASED and means channel 3; its quoted band of 899 is this run's channel 3 exactly, which is what confirms the numbering.

tasks.title: listen.py --files with a path stages nothing, reports success, and writes 11 files into the SID corpus
tasks.verify:
REPRODUCED, WITH THE DAMAGE. `python listen.py <sid_dir> --files C:/full/path/to/5_Title_Tunes.sid --voices -t 120 --presets ../presets.json` printed '5_Title_Tunes.sid staged (named)', 'staged 1 tune(s) -> build\listen' and exited 0, while writing NOTHING to build/listen and 11 files totalling ~85 MB into the SID CORPUS DIRECTORY next to the originals: .h2g.sng, .h2g.sid, .h2g.wav, .original.wav, .trace.json and six per-voice WAVs. They were removed by hand; the corpus is clean and 5_Title_Tunes.sid itself was untouched.

THE MECHANISM IS TWO LINES. `select_names` returns `--files` verbatim, so `r['file']` is the whole path; `stem = name[:-4]` is then an ABSOLUTE path, and `outdir / f'{stem}.h2g.sng'` discards `outdir` entirely -- pathlib's `/` returns the right operand when it is absolute. `src = (sid_dir / name)` survives the same way, which is why the existence check passes and the run looks healthy. `_preset_opts(doc, name)` ALSO misses, because presets.json is keyed on the bare filename, so the tune is converted with defaults rather than its measured options -- the conversion is wrong as well as misplaced (sha 6adcc4cfd3e4 against the correct f5306abedbfa).

A bare `--files 5_Title_Tunes.sid` is correct and was verified in the same session: staged sha f5306abedbfa, written to build/listen, zero stray files in the corpus.

DONE WHEN: a `--files` entry that is a path is either normalised to its basename (and then resolved against sid_dir like every other name) or rejected with a message naming the bare form; a name that matches no presets.json entry is REPORTED rather than silently converted with defaults; and no output path can escape `outdir` -- assert the resolved target is inside it before writing. Tests: a path argument, a bare name, and a name absent from presets.json. THIS CANNOT BE A DOC FIX. The failure is silent and it writes outside the tree it was given, which is the property that made it worth a task rather than a note.

SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT SEEN IN THE SAME SESSION and worth fixing in the same pass: a re-stage of an already-staged tune reuses the existing WAVs (the `out.exists() and size > EMPTY_WAV` guard around listen.py:246), which is deliberate and right for rendering -- but the run then reports 'staged' for a tune whose .sng was never rewritten either, so a stale conversion survives a re-stage that claims to have refreshed it. The .sng write itself is unconditional, so this only bites via the path bug above; check whether it can happen on its own before deciding it is one defect or two.
